title: Unleash the Master Within
coreMove: Find the living stake under the visible topic before shaping any presentation choice.
sourcePressure: The source uses Aimee Mullins, Cameron Russell, Matthieu Ricard, Larry Smith, Melissa Cardon, and Howard Friedman to argue that speaking power starts beneath role or subject, where personal conviction becomes audience-facing energy.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says to be passionate, inspirational, or louder. The useful version asks what the topic means deeply enough that the audience can feel a real stake.

sourceAnchors.name: Aimee Mullins
sourceAnchors.detail: the source says her speaking power comes from a larger commitment to human potential, not from prosthetics as a topic by itself
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Aimee Mullins did not let prosthetics stay a subject; she made them a doorway into possibility and identity.

sourceAnchors.name: Cameron Russell
sourceAnchors.detail: the source says her visible profession gives credibility, but the talk lands because she cares about beauty standards and girls' self-esteem
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Cameron Russell's platform got attention, but her concern about beauty myths gave the attention somewhere serious to go.

sourceAnchors.name: Melissa Cardon's passion research
sourceAnchors.detail: the source cites Cardon's work as support for perceived passion and its effect on audience response
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Passion is not a decorative mood; Cardon's research helps explain why a room reads genuine energy as information.

hook: speaker discovers passion while staring at a blank slide
counterintuition: audiences only care if you care
tryThisNow: write down what you are passionate about
take one minute to find your why
practice saying the topic with enthusiasm

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: a founder whose prototype numbers are solid but whose opening sounds like a market-size memo
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether investors hear another battery dashboard or the reason outages became personal to her
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she moves the first slide after the outage map and opens with the nursing-home hallway where the backup power failed before showing the prototype metrics
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a projector washing a blue outage map across a conference room wall

exampleSpecs.audience: a curator preparing donor remarks about tactile exhibit design
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether donors see ramps and labels as compliance or as access to wonder
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he places a bronze replica in a donor's hand and rewrites the talk around the visitor who could finally feel the sculpture's face
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cool bronze edges resting in a white cotton glove

exampleSpecs.audience: a town engineer presenting seawall options to residents tired of projections
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the room hears cost estimates or the memory of a street that now floods at noon
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she crosses out the technical opener and begins with the tide mark on her father's shop door, then uses the cost table as the answer to that lived stake
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pale salt line across a green shop door

exampleSpecs.audience: a clinical trainer launching a new infusion pump protocol
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether nurses hear another device rollout or a way to prevent one frightening medication delay
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a nurse asks why this pump matters, he answers with the night a dosage alarm gave a team ninety extra seconds, then teaches the buttons
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a plastic pump screen blinking amber beside a coiled IV line
mustAvoid: device specs as the whole point

exampleSpecs.audience: a film student introducing a short documentary about cafeteria workers
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether classmates see a class project or a reason to notice invisible labor on campus
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she cuts the resume-style introduction and starts with the hand-written break schedule that made her realize whose day her film was really about
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grease-spotted break schedule taped beside a steel serving hatch

exampleSpecs.audience: a county official asking a state panel for broadband funds
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the panel hears a connectivity project or the isolation of students doing homework in parked cars
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he moves the speed-test chart to slide three and opens with two headlights outside the library after closing, then connects that image to the grant ask
exampleSpecs.firstImage: headlights glowing in the library parking lot after the doors are locked

skillTargets: separate visible topic from deeper stake
choose an opening that reveals motive without self-display
distinguish genuine passion from volume or theatrics
evaluate whether personal stake has been translated into audience value

tryThisNowSpec: Write your next talk topic in five words, then write the human stake beneath it in one sentence that contains no job title, product name, or credential.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
